rule0_lite.statement: The Wiseman et al. 2026 RSOS supplements (Figshare 32017187 / 32017184) and the article's deposited OpenSim hindlimb models are CC BY 4.0 and API/HTTP-acquirable from this environment without human registration, and the models carry per-muscle path geometry (path points, and possibly PCSA/Fmax) for seven NHP species including a macaque.
rule0_lite.prediction: Per-source predictions below; each falsifier is a concrete observation that would mark the source FAILED or DIVERGENT in download_receipt.json.
rule0_lite.falsifier_policy: Any falsified prediction is recorded honestly in download_receipt.json.divergences and in the lane report. No re-scoping of a source after the fact to make a prediction pass.

sources.route: GET https://api.figshare.com/v2/articles/32017187 (public API, no auth), then download each file's indicated download URL
sources.expectation_from_memo: 1 file named rsos260107_si_001.docx, figshare download id 63739721, license CC BY 4.0; content = muscle homology table across the studied species (maps ~1:1 onto the 36 admitted Guimaraes muscles).
sources.falsifier: API returns a different file count/name/license than the memo recorded, OR the docx contains no muscle-name homology mapping (e.g., prose only, or species set without muscle correspondence).
sources.on_failure: Record actual API payload + sha256 of whatever arrived; if license is not CC BY 4.0 the file is quarantined (not admitted) and the operator is told.

sources.locator: https://doi.org/10.1098/rsos.260107 (RSOS page; memo says bot-blocked from this environment)
sources.route: Try, in order, each step only if the previous fails or yields no model link: (a) direct fetch of the RSOS landing page HTML; (b) PMC open-access mirror (RSOS is OA, PMC deposit expected); (c) Crossref metadata for the license/DAS fields; (d) Figshare search API for author deposits (search 'Wiseman Vereecke OpenSim'); (e) Cambridge Apollo (repo.cam.ac.uk) API search. Follow every automatable data link found in the data-availability statement.
sources.expectation_from_memo: A data-availability statement pointing at a deposited set of OpenSim 4.5 hindlimb .osim models across seven NHP species (one cercopithecoid = macaque), built on a human hindlimb base; the memo could not read the page, so the EXACT repository is unknown (Apollo was the candidate). The models, if open, are the muscle-geometry payload.
sources.falsifier: (a) No data-availability statement reachable by any automatable route -> source stays OPEN with exact hand-download instructions for the operator. (b) Statement found but the model deposit requires registration/login (SimTK-style) -> STOP there, write hand-download instructions, do not attempt to bypass. (c) Statement found, deposit open, but it contains no .osim files (e.g., only the two SIs, or only moment-arm CSVs) -> the memo's 'model files exist publicly' premise is FALSIFIED and recorded as such.
sources.on_failure: Operator hand-download instructions with exact URLs, one line per click.

sources.locator: whatever the article_das route resolves to
sources.route: Plain HTTP download of each .osim (+ Geometry meshes if shipped) from the resolved open repository; sha256 receipt per file per the house pattern (macaque_arm/download_receipt.json shape).
sources.expectation_from_memo: OpenSim 4.5 .osim XML: hindlimb bodies (pelvis..phalanges), per-muscle path points (GeometryPath), possibly wrap objects, Fmax and/or PCSA per muscle, seven species variants incl. one macaque; meshes likely shipped alongside.
sources.falsifier: Files are a different format (Simulink/CDF/FEB), or .osim files without any muscle path points, or species set with no cercopithecoid -> record divergence; inventory reports what actually arrived.
